title: A window 7.0 mm by 6.3 mm
summary: The window keeps the 7.0 mm cut-up and is 6.3 mm high, 44.1 mm^2: with the vent plugged the closed note then solves 90 cents under 340 Hz, so the open vent can trim both ways. It is under the 49 to 60 mm^2 the acoustics notes prefer and over their 36 mm^2 minimum.

rejected.why: the window alone solved at 352 Hz on a 121 cm^3 chamber with a 3.5 mm wall and the full lobe: sharp of 340 Hz with the vent plugged; with the lobe narrowed and a 4 mm wall it was still about 25 cents above, where 60 to 140 cents below is needed for a vent that trims both ways

returns_if.text: when the low note is moved up toward 380 Hz, or the chamber may grow past the 125 cm^3 the design spec allows

rejected.why: the vent-plugged note solved about 41 cents under 340 Hz: short of the 60 cents the tuning step wanted, and of the 50 cents of downward trim that C4 asks for

rejected.value: a deeper window wall (5.5 mm) in place of a lower window
rejected.why: 2 mm more wall lowered the window's conductance only 5 % where 16 % was needed: the passage flares on the ramp side and the lintel side

returns_if.text: not while the passage flares; a straight-sided neck is the throat that lost in the rump-lobe decision

body: The window height is also the width of the air jet. A narrower jet drives the note with less air: the model's estimate of the flow is 9.0 L/min at 200 Pa. No model here predicts loudness; C26 measures it on a printed whistle.
